notes.title: Have You Played… Far Cry Primal?
notes.notes:
Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives. One a day, every day, perhaps for all time.

I’m a sucker for Far Cry’s charismatic bad guys. Since Far Cry 3, Ubisoft has obviously been aiming to write villians that thrill and terrify in equal measure, but with the stone-age Far Cry Primal they weren’t as concerned about handsome, hypnotic lunatics, or superforeigners that were here to save the day via a never-ending stream of bullets.

To my eyes, at least, they wanted to stick Far Cry’s survival of the fittest hunting and gathering in a game where it made sense.

notes.title: How Far Cry 5 can reclaim the open world crown
notes.notes:
Poor Ubisoft. They crafted this enormous open-world icon-riddled niche of their own, trod it into the ground while flogging it to death, and then other people came along, borrowed their ideas, and built superior games with them. In the last year, despite decent showings from Far Cry Primal, The Division, Watch Dogs 2, and Wildlands, players and critics were beginning to weary of yet another open map of odd jobs. None was particularly at fault, but we were experiencing perhaps the sense of diminishing returns, and certainly the weariness of fatigue. And then this year we got Zelda: Breath Of The Wild from Nintendo and Horizon Zero Dawn from Sony. Pow. Two platform-pushing monoliths that schooled Ubisoft at their own games.

In the wake of being so astoundingly outshone, what can Far Cry 5 [official site] do to reclaim the crown?

notes.title: Fan film - Far Cry Primal in real life
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/InG4jO8.png[/img]

DiffView Production [i](FB/diffview.production)[/i] created this fantastic video exploring what Far Cry Primal would have been in real life: 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OCbx1vfADmU
We reached out to them for some behind-the-scenes info.

[img]http://static2.ubi.com/FCPRIMAL/FAN-FILM/Fan-Film_3.gif[/img]
[B]
Far Cry: 
[/B]
Hello! Can you introduce yourself and the DiffView team to the Far Cry community?
[B]
Jirka Klemenc: 
[/B]
DiffView is a small amateur production team from the Czech Republic. We shoot videos based on different computer games especially for the YouTube audience. I started DiffView 3 years ago, and I have the roles of main producer, director, and cameraman. The team includes three other people, and we usually look among our friends for actors, actresses, and helping hands for each new project.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/xvBcme8.jpg[/img]
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
DiffView has created several video game–based films. What was it about Far Cry Primal that made you want to base a film in Oros?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
Before we start the preparation for a game movie, it is essential that one of us already has some kind of a special relationship to it. For Far Cry Primal specifically, this was me: I love animals, beautiful nature, and, of course, action. Far Cry Primal is extraordinarily well-made, looks great visually, and almost begs to have movies made for it.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/jrHb6Lx.jpg[/img]
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
The filming location was beautiful! Could you share with our fans where you filmed?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
It was shot at one of the prettiest places in the Czech Republic - Adršpach, also called the Adršpach Rock Town. When we need a gorgeous location like this, we don’t have to fly over to the US, as we have something this unique right here at our feet.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/YO57pWk.png[/img]
Source - Google Map [i]www.google.ca/maps/@50.6163249,16.0235295,10z[/i]

[B]
FC: 
[/B]
What were the most challenging aspects of making this film?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
Definitely props and costumes that we had to make ourselves. And also health and safety of the actors and stunt people. For example, we had to make a piece of foam look like a rock that you can then safely hit someone in the head with and so on.
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
What sort of research went into the creation of the video?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
Lots and lots of actual playing of the game. Honestly, I have to confess that that’s probably my favorite thing about our work.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/dJSUnDP.jpg[/img]
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
How do you approach your gaming films differently than you do other projects?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
The biggest advantage in making game videos over other types is that the audience usually already knows the game, and so you don’t need to waste time with introductions of the characters and the plot. We can dive straight into action, as there’s not a whole lot of time to spare in short films on YouTube.
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
Do you have advice for other fans who would like to create video content?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
I guess just unleash your fantasy! But also don’t overestimate your capabilities. Only take a challenge not too big for you to handle. And then keep moving forward inch by inch!
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
For our gear and tech fans, what camera(s) did you film with, and what editing software did you use?
[B]
JK: 
[/B]
We used the Black Magic Production Cinema Camera 4K with the SIGMA Art 18-35 f1.8 and Tramon 24-70 f2.8 lenses. For the POV shots, it was, of course, the GoPro 4 Black. The DJI Phantom 2 as our drone and Tascam DR-100 and Rode NTG1 for sound. Editing then took place in Adobe Premiere and Adobe After Effects, the final color grading in DaVinci Resolve.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/0RpuGJu.jpg[/img]
[B]
FC: 
[/B]
Thanks a lot for your answers, Jirka! 
And again, congratulations to the team and actors for this amazing fan film of Far Cry Primal in real life. For more fantastic behind-the-scenes news on the Far Cry Community, check out these articles:

http://steamcommunity.com/games/371660/announcements/detail/704083503709359645

http://steamcommunity.com/games/371660/announcements/detail/967534467972679727

notes.title: Interview - How to finish Survivor Mode + Permadeath
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/sDqDghG.jpg[/img]

We reached out to (one of the few) Far Cry Primal player who finished the game in the highest difficulty setting: [b]Survivor mode[/b] + [b]Permadeath activated[/b] (= only 1 life, no respawn).

Here's the complete interview. 
Enjoy and post your own tips & tricks on how to best play this mode in the comments!

----------------------------

[u][b]How did you feel during your progression in Far Cry Primal’s Survivor mode with Permadeath activated?[/b][/u]

I was scared...

Every single percentage was a huge achievement for me. Every step I made in #Oros felt like reality. I checked areas twice, thrice, and more before taking a step forward. I realized soon (at approximately 2% progression) that I was the prey and not the super-imba-hero anymore.

But because my first try of Survivor mode plus Permadeath was after 130 hours of regular gameplay, I already knew what could happen. I tried Survivor mode three times before finishing it. For the Survivor mode plus Permadeath activated run, it took me approximately 16 tries!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/vk2pS2Z.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Impressive. Congrats on completing it! Can you introduce yourself to the community?[/b][/u]

Hi, my name is Pan and I am a 40-year-old passionate PC gamer from Germany living in Dubai. I have been into gaming – especially RPGs – since the dark ages. It all started with pen and paper games (AD&D, RuneQuest, etc.). My first MMRPG was Lord British’s Ultima Online in the ‘90s. Great times – I remember paying 100 EUR one month for a dial-in connection; my parents almost killed me!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/nOVVUbF.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Ok so what suggestions would you give to someone who wants to try Survivor mode + Permadeath?[/b][/u]

[list]
    [*] Slow and careful! You are not the hero but the prey in this mode! 
    [*] Use every possible easy sidequest to get points and add perks; they will save your life later! 
    [*] Take your time; double check places with your Owl.
    [*] When you reach the point when you fight Batari, use Berserk bombs with your upgraded Hunter’s belt on her fighters.
    [*] Never forget that you can die every single moment in Survivor, and if this happens put the game aside for a few hours and start all over after a coffee break (happened to me many times).
[/list]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/OAgUPpt.jpg[/img]

[u][b]What were your biggest challenges / scariest moments?[/b][/u]

The fight against Batari! That moment when the song “The Wolf” (Fever Ray) starts playing…oh god, my heart starts beating faster even now. 

Second, I would say the first time you meet a sabretooth tiger in Sayla’s quest (it killed me three times!).

[img]http://i.imgur.com/hIcRoag.jpg[/img]

[u][b]What weapons did you use most in this mode?[/b][/u]

Well, I mainly used the longbow from the moment it was available with Jayma. This weapon saved my *** so many times. I upgraded it ASAP.

Next was the spear for close-distance throws. I always avoided close enemy contact in that brutal mode. The good thing was that you could quickly upgrade your melee weapons and the hybrid (spear), while with the longbow you had to wait much longer for a full upgrade with Jayma.

I know some Permadeath Survivor players avoided the multiple-kill perk upgrade. But I used it. It was important in some situations, especially when there was no way to avoid confrontation, like in Ull’s caves.

But still, my best weapon was the sneaky takedown/stealthkill...as you can see in the image below (look at the stat "# Stealth Kills").

[img]http://i.imgur.com/TQWPJXc.jpg[/img]

[u][b]What about the perks, which ones did you use to help your progression? Which ones are important?[/b][/u]

Oh, this is easy...to survive in Survivor/Permadeath you will need all the [b]life[/b], [b]stamina[/b] and [b]healing[/b] you can get!

So prioritize perks that increase:
a) your life.
b) your stamina (to run away).
c) healing skills.

I put all my effort toward increasing these perks in Survivor/Permadeath from the very beginning, so I was even saving points to increase my life bar to the max (three bars only) after saving Karoosh.

[u][b]Ok and what were your biggest achievements and wow moments?[/b][/u]

Killing Ull and Batari in Permadeath and watching the Far Cry Champion “The End” Video  from the Dev team: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cwH5-hUljM

And also the Dream "Batari’s Fear" where you shoot the moon! :)

[img]http://i.imgur.com/SOETPhn.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Which beasts did you use most during your adventure?[/b][/u]

In Survivor/Permadeath mode it was the black tiger – I was too scared to try to tame the sabretooth or the cave bear. It was very difficult to bring him down to 50% to tame him, a lesson I learned in prior attempts in this mode.

[u][b]Thanks for all the useful advice! Any other last words?[/b][/u]

Thanks to the Dev team for this game, because frankly speaking, Far Cry Primal Survivor/Permadeath was the most intense gaming experience I’ve ever had. Also, thanks for the #Wenja language, which is the most amazing language, created by two great linguists (the Byrds)! This language helped me a lot to immerse myself into the game, and it increased the fantastic game experience. You can find their website here: https://speakingprimal.blogspot.ca/
And their Twitter is: http://twitter.com/speakingprimal

Now only a VR experience with this mode could top it. I am up for this challenge! ;-D

[img]http://i.imgur.com/9VTyU53.jpg[/img]

[i]All screenshot in this article were made by Pantelis. you can find his other pics here: http://imgur.com/a/mHwt9[/i]

notes.title: Fantastic Batari Cosplay and interview
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/V5AMJV1.jpg[/img]

[i]The Far Cry community team was amazed when they spotted this awesome Batari cosplay. We reached out to its creator to ask her some questions and pick her nerdy brain.[/i]

[b]Hi there, can you present yourself to the Far Cry community?[/b]

Hi! I'm Scarlett from [url=https://www.facebook.com/scarlettcostuming]Scarlett Costuming and Art (FB link)[/url], but my real name is Emilie. 
I'm a Danish cosplayer and biologist in the making. I'm currently writing my Master's thesis on ancient DNA from humans from the Ice Age, and that might be why I fell in love with Far Cry Primal – as a scientist I'm very interested in ancient people and their way of life, so when I saw that Far Cry Primal was a thing, I added it straight to my games list. I watched my brother play Far Cry 3, but I only just joined the Far Cry ranks when I got into Far Cry Primal.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/i0ZsSIi.jpg[/img]

[b]That’s pretty unique! And what about your cosplaying skills?[/b]

I have been cosplaying for two years! I'm still quite new in the cosplay community and I'm still learning with every costume, but I love it. It's such a creative hobby and I love to create wearable art – it's the best! I also love being on stage and performing, and I have represented Denmark at [url=http://www.eurocosplay.com/]EuroCosplay[/url] in London, which was an amazing experience! I could go on and on about cosplay as a hobby, it's so much fun. I have been attending contests for as long as I have been cosplaying, and just recently I won first at Dreamhack Summer 2016 in Sweden (picture credits: Danarki).

[img]http://i.imgur.com/QnampBJ.jpg[/img]

[b]Wow, congratulations! How was your experience of these competitions?[/b]

Thank you! I wore Amiri of the Six Bears from Pathfinder for the finals at EuroCosplay 2015, and I have had such a great reaction from fans of Pathfinder. I play Dungeons & Dragons myself, so it was so cool to actually make one of the iconic characters in real life. Only a few people have recognized the cosplay, but some did when I wore her at Dreamhack Winter 2015 and won second place. I love bonding over a character like that when meeting fans of the franchise! (I have attached two pictures of Amiri, if you want to see that, too! It's the barbarian lady.)
I wore the Empress of Bones from Asura Online for the competition at Dreamhack Summer 2016, and the judges were so nice at the pre-judging. I wasn't able to wear the bone wings at the pre-judging, but I wore them on stage for my small performance, and they said they loved it, so I couldn't be happier about it. :) It's a tough costume to wear, but so worth it!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/BuRsrli.jpg[/img]

[b]Ok, that’s pretty impressive. But why Batari?[/b]

I chose Batari because of her fierceness and her amazing design. I have always loved big headdresses, and when I saw her in game, my initial reaction was "gotta cosplay her." Then I saw she wasn't wearing a top and I knew I had to tweak the design a bit. ;) She's a tough and cold-hearted woman, but I really love how she doesn't bow down to anyone and that she's a very strong woman. She's got her priorities a bit mixed up and she rules with an iron fist, but hey, we can all have a bad day.

In short: she's a very well-written character and she looks so majestic and imposing that I couldn't resist. I usually gravitate towards dark and strong characters.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/UVqumnQ.jpg[/img]

[b]And how long did it take you to get the final version of the costume?[/b]

I finished the cosplay in six days. I made the decision quite late before the deadline, so I had to work on the cosplay a lot, but I didn't mind. I was trying out new materials and techniques, and I really love how it turned out, so I had fun!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/8JnZYkT.jpg[/img]

[b]What were the most difficult parts?[/b]

The headdress and the wig were quite challenging. I'm a blonde and I needed to make sure the dreads would cover my hair and not break the illusion. So I made a fake hairline of dreads I back-combed myself. The biggest issue ended up being the sheer weight of the headdress and dreads since everything had to stay on my head by itself. I solved this with multiple hairclips (ow!) and elastic bands. I also glued down the hairline with some prosthetic skin glue to make sure it didn't slide back.

[b]What material did you use for it?[/b]

The headdress is made from beach mats! I bought some very cheap ones and painted liquid latex and glue on one side to make sure the woven straw didn't simply fall apart when I cut them into strips. Then I "braided" the strips of straw into the texture from the game (I used a lot of screenshots from the game and the concept art to make sure I replicated everything as closely as possible to the source material) and glued it onto a base I made from thermoplastic. Later I wove string onto the back part of the headdress and weathered the whole thing. I did the same for the bracers and shin guards. The rest of the costume was leather I had lying around from previous cosplays.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/1X6N2J5.jpg[/img]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/UvTUHfC.jpg[/img]

[b]Do you have any advice for other Far Cry fans who’d like to start their own cosplay?[/b]

These kinds of cosplays are amazing to craft! You don't need to be precise and have a perfect technique or perfect craftsmanship; the materials are all natural, and everything is rugged and dirty. It's really interesting to create something new that has to look old – so my advice would be to weather everything thoroughly to make it appear old. It's all about creative solutions like using coffee or tea to make leathers look old and stained, or using a wash of acrylics to make the straw look a bit dirty and worn by time. Weathering is everything in cosplays like these. :)

[img]http://i.imgur.com/gPgvKRg.jpg[/img]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/zAEGSgA.jpg[/img]

[b]What did you think about the Wenja language that we used for the game?[/b]

I loved the Wenja language! Very guttural and primal: it seems very plausible for it to sound like that! I would not be very qualified to comment on the correctness, though. ;) I work with extracting ancient DNA from petrous bones (ear bones) and mapping the genes of the people in the population. Super interesting and very nerdy!

[b]Would you like to share anything else about this project or the game?[/b]

Keep making games like these, lol. It makes my nerdy scientist heart happy.

notes.title: Far Cry Primal - Patch 1.3.0 Notes (Introducing Survivor Mode!)
notes.notes:
[img=https://scontent-atl3-1.xx.fbcdn.net/t31.0-8/12823502_439321916275205_2854460059997217194_o.jpg]

Fellow Wenja, 

We’re happy to announce the release of the new [b]Patch 3[/b] available on PS4, Xbox One and PC. It is available for free on April 12, 2016 and includes the below changes. 

Patch 3 download size: 
- PC (1.1 GB) 
- PS4 (849 MB) 
- Xbox One (817 MB) 

A second PC-specific free update, the [b]Ultra-HD Texture[/b] pack, can be downloaded separately. It adds high-quality textures to the PC version of the game. 

[b]HD Texture Pack download size:[/b][list] 
[*]PC only (3.5 GB)
[*]Separate download available on Steam or Uplay[/list]

[b]Patch Notes – Patch 3[/b]

1. [b]NEW – Survivor Mode[/b][list]
[*]Available in New Gameplay Options when starting a New Game[/list]

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_StaminaBar_small_246447.jpg]

b. [b]NEW[/b] – Stamina Bar added [list]
[*]Stamina depletes slowly during gameplay 
[*]Stamina depletes faster when walking/running/being in combat 
[*]Fast travel consumes stamina 
[*]Stamina can be regenerated by sleeping and eating food 
[*]Manual heal and fast travel costs stamina 
[*]Low stamina slows down movement and health regen. At 0 stamina, manual heal and fast travel are disabled. [/list]

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_Exploration_small_246449.jpg]

c. Tamed Beasts [olist]
[*][b]NEW[/b] – Permadeath for Tamed Beasts [list]
[*]If a Beast dies, the player must find and tame a new one 
[*]This also applies to Legendary Beasts, they can never be found again if they die 
[*]Skinning a Beast after they die gives you a skin [/list]
[*][b]NEW[/b] – Beast riding fatigue introduced – After some time of continuous riding, mounted Beast will start taking damage 
[*]In order to activate the taming option for Sabretooth Tigers, Brown Bears and Cave Bears, you must first inflict them serious damage 
[*]Non-legendary tamed Beasts health has been reduced 
[*]Owl attacks and bomb drops have been disabled [/olist]

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_ExpertDifficulty_small_246450.jpg]

d. World/Resources [list]
[*]Less natural resources are available in the world and less are looted when gathering 
[*]Less daily resources added to the Reward Stash from Wenja population level 
[*]Resources in the Reward Stash can only be withdrawn at the Village Stash 
[*]Night lasts longer and is darker 
[*]Campfire Fast Travel points are no longer unlocked by default when claiming a bonfire [/list]

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_CompanionChanges_small_246452.jpg]

e. Skills [list]
[*]XP Curve has been adjusted to be more progressive 
[*]Certain “over-powered” skills have been removed:[/list][olist]
[*]Player skills:[list]
[*]Extra Health II 
[*]Primitive Heal II 
[*]Extra Health IV[/list]
[*]Gatherer skills:[list]
[*]Show Plants 
[*]Show Resources 
[*]Beast Reviving[/list]
[*]Hunter skills:[list]
[*]Craft Arrows III[/list]
[*]Shaman skills:[list]
[*]Owl – Weapon drop 
[*]Owl – Attack I 
[*]Owl – Attack II 
[*]Owl – Cooldown I 
[*]Owl – Cooldown II[/list][/olist][list]
[*]Effects of other skills have been re-balanced 
[*]Skill points cost has been rebalanced [/list][olist]
[*]Player skills:[list]
[*]Primitive Heal I: 2 points instead of 1 
[*]Extra Health I: 3 points instead of 1 [/list]
[*]Gatherer skills: [list]
[*]Skinning II: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Find Resources I: 3 points instead of 1 
[*]Skinning I: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Find Rare Plants: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Find Resources II: 4 points instead of 2 
[*]Find Rare Resources: 3 points instead of 2 [/list]
[*]Crafter Skills: [list]
[*]Double Clubs: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Double Spears: 4 points instead of 3 
[*]Double Traps: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Double Sting Bombs: 4 points instead of 2 
[*]Double Bait: 2 points instead of 1[/list] 
[*]Hunter skills: [list]
[*]Craft Arrows I: 3 points instead of 1 
[*]Craft Arrows II: 5 points instead of 2 
[*]Tag Enemies: 2 points instead of 1 [/list]
[*]Shaman skills: [list]
[*]Tame Wildcats: 2 points instead of 1 
[*]Tame Apex Predators: 3 points instead of 2 
[*]Tame Cunning Beasts: 4 points instead of 3 [/list]
[*]Warrior skills: [list]
[*]Heavy Takedown: 4 points instead of 3 
[*]Extra Health III: 6 points instead of 4 [/list][/olist]

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_NightTime_small_246448.jpg]

f. Gameplay [list]
[*]Bow tension added requiring players to pull back the arrow all the way to get maximum impact 
[*]Weapon durability has been tweaked to be more realistic when thrown weapons hit hard or soft surfaces 
[*]Weapons are consumed more quickly by fire 
[*]The slow-motion time effect doesn’t slow time as much anymore, when in the Weapon Wheel, Food Grid and Beast Grid 
[*]Crafting ammo in the Weapon Wheel now requires a hold to craft 
[*]Most bag capacity has been reduced 
[*]Player’s health regen speed has been reduced 
[*]Some healing recipes now require red leaves in addition to green leaves 
[*]Cold depletion rate has been increased 
[*]Fully upgraded Winter Clothes no longer offer total protection from the cold 
[*]Weapons on fire will extinguish when swapping between weapons (Expert difficulty only) 
[*]Fast Travel now costs Stamina and Meat, proportionally to distance 
[*]Mini-map has been removed 
[*]Shaders on tagged enemies have been removed, making them more difficult to spot 
[*]Several UI options have been set to off by default to increase immersion (but can be re-enabled) 
[*]Hunter Vision duration has been set to 20s by default (duration can now be modified in the settings) 
[*]Fog of war reveal radius has been reduced 
[*]Can only Save & Quit when not in Combat 
[*]Game difficulty cannot be changed once started in Survivor Mode with Permadeath 
[*]Requirements for rare animal skins have been reduced when upgrading huts 
[*]Reduced health for Legendary Beasts, Batari and Ull[/list] 

[img=http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-US/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Infographic_Crafting_small_246451.jpg]

g. AI/Wildlife [list]
[*]Enemies are more reactive and aggressive in combat 
[*]Wildlife detects you more easily 
[*]Blood trails from wounded animals are harder to track 
[*]Reduced overall animal density during the day, and increased density of predators at night 
[*]Reduced human density and frequency of Wenja events 
[*]Wenja fighters are less resilient 
[*]Predators no longer show up in Hunter Vision unless they are aggressive toward the player, dead or a Tamed Beast[/list]

2. [b]NEW – Permadeath [/b][list]
[*]Available in New Gameplay Options when starting a New Game with Survivor Mode turned On 
[*]Three Options Available – Off, On, Second Chance [olist]
[*]Off – You respawn when you die 
[*]On – The game is over when you die 
[*]Second Chance – You only respawn if you completed enough of the game since your last death (every 3% as depicted in the player’s overall progress) [/olist]
[*]Failing during Tensay’s Vision missions does not count as dying (You’re dreaming after all)[/list]

3. Stability and Performance [list]
[*]a. Fixed an issue where player could lose their inventory when swapping weapons in specific conditions 
[*]b. Fixed some specific, low occurrence crashes[/list]

4. Gameplay [list]
[*][b]New Option[/b] in Gameplay Menu – [b]Hunter Vision Duration[/b] – Can toggle the duration of Hunter Vision (Default/20s/30s/Infinite) 
[*][b]New Option[/b] in the Interface Menu – Hide the bow reticle unless you are aiming or holding the bow ready 
[*]Fixed melee damage resistance skill also affecting ranged damage 
[*]Increased critical health in hard/expert difficulty modes[/list]

5. Lighting and FX [list]
[*]Fixed a lighting issue on bodies of water that would cause color to briefly change when exiting caves 
[*]Minor fixes to clipping issues[/list]

6. Wildlife and AI [list]
[*]Various bug fixes[/list]

7. Missions/Activities/World [list]
[*]Fixed a grapple location north of Tushwarha Outpost that would cause the player to fall to his death when trying to climb down 
[*]Fixed an issue where players could exit the map in the mission – Vision of Ice 
[*]Fixed an issue where players could exit the map in Shayu’s Cave 
[*]Fixed a couple issues where players could get stuck in the Dangu Cave 
[*]Fixed an issue where players could get stuck in an infinite death loop after completing the mission – Into Udam Land 
[*]Fixed some resources that would cause the player to become stuck in the map when gathering them 
[*]Fixed an issue where Bite Fish weren’t spawning in certain locations on the map 
[*]Fixed an issue where player could get stuck in the falling obelisk outside of the Batari’s Temple in the Izila Homeland[/list]

8. Menu/UI/Map [list]
[*]Fixed an issue that would cause one of the life bars to flicker in specific conditions 
[*]Fixed an issue where a “Location Discovered” prompt would remain on screen during cut-scenes in specific situations 
[*]Fixed an issue where some icons remained on screen when using the “Turn All Off” option in the Interface menu[/list]

9. [b]NEW – 4x Achievements and Ubisoft Club badges[/b] [list]
[*]Achievement #1: TOP OF THE FOOD CHAIN [list]
[*]Finish the game in the Survivor mode (Any difficulty). [/list]
[*]Achievement #2: TOP OF THE FOOD CHAIN (2ND CHANCE) [list]
[*]Finish the game in the Survivor mode (Any difficulty) and the Second chance option activated.[/list]
[*]Achievement #3: TOP OF THE FOOD CHAIN (PERMADEATH)[list]
[*]Finish the game in the Survivor mode (Any difficulty) and the Permadeath option activated. [/list]
[*]Achievement #4: SURVIVAL OF THE FITTEST [list]
[*]Finish the game in Survivor mode (Expert difficulty) and the Permadeath option activated... Forget it… No-one will ever achieve it.[/list][/list]

10. [b]NEW – PC fixes and support for Ultra-HD Texture Pack[/b] [list]
[*]NEW – Support for ultra-HD texture pack (Note: PC Patch 3 does not include the texture pack. It can be downloaded separately for free on Steam or Uplay.)
[*]PC-specific fixes: [list]
[*]Add option to turn off mouse deadzones 
[*]Interface and input tweaks 
[*]Various minor bug fixes[/list][/list]

notes.title: Announcing Survivor Mode for Far Cry Primal
notes.notes:
[img]http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-GB/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Survivor_Logo_Final_245485.jpg[/img]

Far Cry Primal is about to become a lot more ruthless. A brutal new way to play, Survivor Mode, will arrive as a free patch on April 12. Included with this update will also be a high stakes permadeath option. Enabling permadeath means your game is over the first time you die.

[img]http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-GB/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Primal_Mode_concept1_small_245487.jpg[/img]

Permadeath is only the beginning. Survivor mode adds a stamina gauge, the minimap is now turned off by default, and the fog of war has been strengthened. Even fast travel is a little tougher, as it now consumes stamina and food.

To top it all off, taming beasts is becoming much more difficult. Some animals will need to be brought down to half-life before they can be baited and tamed. Make sure to take care of your pets since animals who die are gone for good. While you can always tame another leopard or wolf, creatures like the Bloodfang Sabretooth can't ever be brought back once lost.

[img]http://static9.cdn.ubi.com/resource/en-GB/game/far-cry/primal/FCP_Primal_Mode_concept2_small_245488.jpg[/img]

If you go for the ultimate challenge – activating Survivor mode, playing on expert difficulty and activating permadeath – you have the hardest and most insane challenge possible for the game. There's a special reward at the moment you complete the game for anyone insane enough to complete this challenge. Survivor mode will be available as a free patch for PlayStation 4, Xbox One and PC on April 12th.

Tune in on April 7th to watch the exclusive first look at the survivor mode on http://www.twitch.tv/ubisoft

Can you survive?

https://youtu.be/YgBvIboq-YM

notes.title: Playing Far Cry Primal Like A True Caveman
notes.notes:
When Far Cry Primal [official site] was unveiled, I shrugged with semi-feigned disinterest, aware that the series has hit milking point, but unable to dismiss the inner teenager tugging at my inner sleeve saying But – but it’s got cavemen and tribes and woolly mammoths and – and you can ride them, and throw spears and stuff! Yes, the prehistoric era taps into a primal fantasy in me, but when that’s overlaid with an advanced radar, an owl endowed with the abilities of a military drone, and heat-vision that conveniently colour-codes every object, footprint and smell, the fantasy kind of tapers off.

By shutting off as many aids and HUD elements as possible, I intended to reclaim the fantasy.

notes.title: Far Cry Primal PC System Requirements
notes.notes:
Today, Ubisoft announced the PC specs for Far Cry Primal, which will be available on February 23rd for PS4 and Xbox One and on March 1st for PC. Below is a full list of the system requirements.


[B]MINIMUM[/B]

[B]Supported OS[/B]
Windows 7, Windows 8.1, Windows 10 (64-bit versions only)

[B]Processor[/B]
Intel Core i3-550 | AMD Phenom II X4 955 or equivalent

[B]RAM[/B]
4GB

[B]Video Card[/B]
NVIDIA GeForce GTX 460 (1GB VRAM) | AMD Radeon HD 5770 (1GB VRAM) or equivalent 

[B]Hard Disk Space[/B]
20 GB

[B]Peripherals[/B]
Windows-compatible keyboard, mouse, optional controller


[B]RECOMMENDED[/B]

[B]Supported OS[/B]
Windows 7, Windows 8.1, Windows 10 (64-bit versions only)

[B]Processor[/B]
Intel Core i7-2600K | AMD FX-8350 or equivalent

[B]RAM[/B]
8GB

[B]Video Card[/B]
NVIDIA GeForce GTX 780 | AMD Radeon R9 280X or equivalent

[B]Hard Disk Space[/B]
20 GB

[B]Peripherals[/B]
Windows-compatible keyboard, mouse, optional controller


[B]Supported Video Cards at Release[/B]

AMD Radeon™ HD 5770 (1 GB VRAM) or better, HD 7000 / 200  / 300 / Fury X series
NVIDIA® GeForce® GTX 460 (1 GB VRAM) or better, GTX 500 / 600 / 700 / 900 / TITAN series

[B]Note[/B]: This product supports 64-bit operating systems only. Laptop versions of these cards may work, but are not officially supported. For the most up-to-date requirement listings, please visit the FAQ on our support website at support.ubi.com.

Welcome to the Stone Age, a time of extreme danger and limitless adventure, when giant mammoths and sabretooth tigers ruled the Earth and humanity is at the bottom of the food chain.
